Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up / next steps (Acme Analytics)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before Marcus and I put together a tailored capacity recommendation and estimate. Please confirm any corrections.

Summary of needs
- Primary workload: customer-facing summarization and retrieval-augmented generation for support workflows.
- Models under consideration: gpt-large-1 / open-llama-13b (prefers lower-latency variant).
- Typical request size: ~200–300 tokens.
- Expected baseline: ~100M tokens/month. Peak/target: ~1B tokens/month during product launch windows.
- Latency target: p50 < 150ms for generation token stream (interactive experience).
- Peak throughput target: ~10,000 tokens/sec (burstable).

Key pricing/contract questions for your team
1) Target unit economics: what range are you thinking for cost per 1M tokens? (helps choose Dedicated config vs hosted + burst)
2) Budget range for reserved capacity (monthly committed spend)?
3) Any hard constraints on GPU type (e.g., must be H100) or flexibility to consider A100/8x M10-like configs?

Next steps
- Marcus will propose an initial sizing (GPU type + # of GPUs) and a back-of-envelope unit cost ($/1M tokens) based on the expected profile.
- If that looks good, we can set a technical deep-dive with your infra team and pull a draft contract/PO annex for procurement.

Attachments: draft MA (for reference) and a quick capacity worksheet (we'll populate after Marcus' sizing).

Thanks — talk soon,

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary, looks accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Model: leaning toward gpt-large-1 for quality/latency tradeoff. We may try an open-variant for cost testing but production will be gpt-large-1.
- Tokens: baseline 100M/month is correct; launch window could push sustained to ~500–700M for 4–6 weeks, with short spikes up to ~1B/month.
- Throughput: our product team expects to sustain ~6k tokens/sec during peak and allow bursts to ~12k tokens/sec for short periods.
- Budget: procurement gave a rough target of $60–$80 per 1M tokens (total cost to the business, including infra). They asked us to validate whether Dedicated reserved capacity can hit that target.
- GPU preference: Priya (CTO) prefers H100 if it materially improves latency/cost; open to A100 if the numbers are similar.

Next: Marcus — would love a recommended config (GPU type + count) and a back-of-envelope MSP (monthly spend) + unit $/1M tokens. Also please flag any pagination/streaming tradeoffs that affect the latency numbers.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up / initial sizing & unit economics

Jordan / Marissa — quick sizing note and cost model based on the numbers you provided. This is a conservative back-of-envelope we can refine after we see traces/real qps.

Assumptions used
- Model: gpt-large-1, ~70B-ish param behavior for inference profile (KV cache utilization considered).
- Avg tokens per request: 250 (to be validated).
- Target sustained peak: 6k tokens/sec; burst capacity to 12k tokens/sec.
- Effective utilization: aiming ~70% to keep latency SLOs stable.

Sizing recommendation (reserved pool)
- GPU: H100 80GB recommended for best latency per token on gpt-large-1 (attention and fp8 kernels).
- Baseline reserved: 4x H100 (reserved) + 1x H100 burstable (shared pool) — estimated sustained throughput ~10–12k tokens/sec depending on batching and sampling temp.
- If A100 80GB is mandated, recommend 6x A100 to reach similar sustained throughput (A100 has lower perf on fp8 kernels for this architecture).

Cost / unit economics (very rough)
- Estimated monthly reserved infra cost (list rates + Redwood infra margin): H100 4x reserved ~ $135,000/month (includes support/ops). With a burstable node add ~ $30k/month in peak allowances.
- If you run at ~400M tokens/month average (between baseline + launch smoothing), that implies ~ $337.5 per 1M tokens purely on infra (this is conservative high because we left headroom).
- With higher utilization and capacity tuning (better batching, KV cache hits) we can push unit cost down materially. Practical targeted unit economics we can achieve with tuning: $60–$80 per 1M tokens (this includes Redwood managed runtime, observability + modest margin) — aligns with your procurement target *if* you commit to reserved capacity and we reach ~800M+ monthly effective tokens throughputs during the term.

Tradeoffs / notes
- The biggest lever is utilization: improving caching and predictable request shapes reduces effective cost per token (we can run an eval to estimate caching hit-rate).
- H100 wins on latency and reduces GPU count required; A100 increases capital needing more reserved units.
- If budget is tight, we can explore mixed strategy: Dedicated baseline (2x H100) + hosted API for burst and non-critical traffic — reduces committed cost but increases per-token hosted costs.

Attachments: capacity_estimate.xlsx (breakdown by GPU, throughput slices) and a draft quote (Acme_MA_Draft.pdf).

If this direction looks good I can: (a) run a short perf test on a representative prompt set; (b) lock in a draft reserved quote for procurement; (c) schedule infra deep-dive next week.

—Marcus
